purpose: Identify retained/event/control/basis/compiler contributions to the fixed four-case compiled RZ reversal; no population or N/G result
minimum_prior_approval: Explicit approval for each selected diagnostic's saved-input circuit construction, finite compilation and diagnostic arithmetic; flags alone cannot activate this draft

fixed.system: linear H4 1A STO-3G n8, common saved state not evolved
fixed.compiler: old Qiskit1.3.0 rz/sx/x/cx opt1 seed17, no coupling/backend/layout/routing

preconditions: Implement and artificially test replay from saved event/primitive descriptors without RNG, eigensolver or preparation regeneration. If original builder requires extra scientific preparation, STOP and return scope.
Freeze new diagnostic SOURCE/runtime/input SHA and separate invalid-to-valid grant only after explicit approval. Never reuse a consumed grant.
Carry every constant, extracted identity, negative product and order phase as ancilla-relative phase. Preserve gate order, basis identity and signs.
Check rebuilt full input fingerprints and compiled RZ against old matching case/trajectory. A mismatch ends the diagnostic; do not silently replace old result or call new program historical evidence.

Own output/claim/receipt/native exit/reap/STOP. Monitor resources without killing healthy workers for transient shared CPU/PSI contention. Existing immutable inputs only; no unrelated-worktree freeze.

designs.question: Does retained cost floor or event realization explain PR gap; how nonadditive is full compilation?
designs.selection: PF singleton in each representation; PR trajectory_index=0 in each representation fixed before new diagnostic. No cost extremum selection; no cohort-representativeness claim.
outputs: before-control body and after-control / pretranspile / posttranspile gate histograms
source category tags with nested basis/control marked; no double counting
input/output QPY or QASM and exact fingerprints
full-vs-isolated interaction residual with explicit repeated-wrapper/phase convention
designs.limits: Isolated ablations change unitary and cannot be ranked as valid original PF/PR algorithms. Marginal costs do not give unique additive causal attribution. Old full-circuit price must reproduce before use. No actual efficiency/accuracy/population claim.

designs.depends_on: D1 Pauli full baselines and phase-preserving artificial tests
designs.question: How much does Pauli generic whole-body control plus compiler response cost versus equivalent central-rotation control?
designs.selection: Same saved Pauli PF and PR index0 as D1
variants: phase-preserving specialized controlled Pauli PF full
phase-preserving specialized controlled Pauli PR index0 full
outputs: algebraic control identity and artificial phase checks
same-body old-control/new-control gate histograms and compiled metrics/programs
designs.limits: New implementation series; no update to old measured values. Neither result identifies representation-only effect.

designs.depends_on: D1 DF PR index0 baseline; evidence that adjacent equal-basis reuse actually removes a pair
designs.question: How much is saved by already-active DF builder basis reuse?
designs.selection: Same saved DF PR index0; do not select another trajectory if no reuse opportunity
variants: DF PR full with only cancel_adjacent_equal_bases disabled
outputs: paired equal-body proof and basis counters
designs.skip_condition: No removable equal-basis pair in D1 => no D3 circuit/compile. Record no contrast in this trajectory; do not search for another.
designs.limits: No boundary optimization or support-restricted basis, no prefix change, no mean inference. Does not isolate all basis cost.

deferred_new_series: Prefix/law sensitivity only after physical matched-criterion design; equality of prefix counts is not a fair control. Not part of D1-D3.
resources: No arbitrary low CPU/RAM/worker caps; choose efficient computational concurrency within selected finite call budgets. No OS/shared environment/other-user changes.
exit: Mandatory STOP per selected diagnostic; no automatic transition to another design.
